input.content:
# Notifications

Sends one message to one user over email, SMS, Slack or an in-app inbox. Each
channel validates the recipient, applies throttling, formats a payload and passes
it to a transport function you supply.

## Usage

```js
const { createNotifier, createAllNotifiers, registry } = require('./src/notifications');

const email = createNotifier('email', {
  transport: { email: async payload => mailer.send(payload) },
  from: 'alerts@example.com'
});

await email.send(
  { id: 'u1', name: 'Ava', email: 'ava@example.com' },
  { title: 'Hello {{name}}', body: 'Your report is ready', category: 'transactional' }
);
// { channel: 'email', status: 'sent', userId: 'u1', id: 'email-u1-<ms>', preview: 'Your report is ready' }

await email.send(
  { id: 'u1', email: 'ava@example.com' },
  { title: 'Sale', body: '20% off', category: 'marketing' }
);
// { channel: 'email', status: 'throttled', reason: 'user has not opted into marketing email', retryAt: null, userId: 'u1' }
```

`createAllNotifiers(options)` returns `{ email, sms, slack, inapp }`, all built
from the same options. `registry` maps each channel name to its factory.

`send(user, message, options)` rejects with a `TypeError` for invalid input and
with an `Error` when the channel's transport function is missing or fails. A
throttled message resolves with `status: 'throttled'` and is not delivered.

## Layout

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `index.js` | Public API: `createNotifier`, `createAllNotifiers`, `registry` |
| `composeNotifier.js` | Builds a notifier from a channel strategy and runs the send pipeline |
| `validation.js` | Recipient and message checks shared by every channel |
| `throttling.js` | Hourly limit, exemption and consent rules, plus the delivery record |
| `formatting.js` | Placeholder substitution and the envelope every payload starts from |
| `delivery.js` | Hands a payload to `transport[<channel>]` |
| `channels/*.js` | One strategy per channel |

## How `send` runs

1. `validateRecipient(user)`, then the channel's `validateUser(user)`.
2. `validateMessage(message)`.
3. The channel's throttle rules, in order. A throttled verdict returns early.
4. `formatEnvelope` builds the shared fields (`id`, `locale`, `title`, `body`,
   `preview`, `metadata`), then the channel's `format` adds its own.
5. The channel's `deliver` awaits the transport.
6. `recordDelivery` stores the send time for the hourly limit.

A delivery is recorded only after the transport resolves, so a failed delivery
does not count against the limit.

## Channel strategies

A strategy is a frozen object:

```js
{
  name: 'sms',
  defaultMaxPerHour: 4,
  resolveSettings: options => ({ senderId: options.senderId || 'APP', ... }),
  validateUser: user => { /* throw TypeError */ },
  throttleRules: [hourlyLimit, requireMarketingConsent('smsOptIn', '...')],
  format: (envelope, { config, user, message, options }) => ({ ...envelope, ... }),
  deliver: deliverVia('sms', 'sms')
}
```

Settings and defaults. Every default is applied with `||`, so `0` and `''`
fall back to it.

| Scope | Setting (default) |
| --- | --- |
| All channels | `transport` (`{}`), `throttleStore` (new `Map` per notifier), `now` (`() => new Date()`), `defaultLocale` (`'en-US'`), `defaultSender` (`'Product Team'`), `templates` (`{}`), `maxPerHour` (channel default below) |
| email, max 8/h | `from` (`noreply@example.com`), `replyTo` (`support@example.com`), `unsubscribeBaseUrl` (`https://example.com/unsubscribe`) |
| sms, max 4/h | `senderId` (`APP`), `segmentLength` (`140`) |
| slack, max 20/h | `defaultWorkspace` (`main`), `defaultChannel` (`#general`) |
| inapp, max 50/h | `defaultIcon` (`bell`), `defaultAction` (`/notifications`) |

Throttle rules per channel. A rule returns a verdict to stop evaluation or `null`
to pass to the next one. If every rule passes, the message is sent.

| Channel | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| email | `hourlyLimit`, then `requireMarketingConsent('emailOptIn')` |
| sms | `hourlyLimit`, then `requireMarketingConsent('smsOptIn')` |
| slack | `exemptWhen(options.threadTs)`, then `hourlyLimit` |
| inapp | `exemptWhen(message.category === 'security')`, then `hourlyLimit` |

`hourlyLimit` counts sends per channel, user id and category over a sliding hour.
It skips `force: true` and `priority: 'urgent'` sends. Because the consent rule
comes after it, an urgent or forced marketing message still needs opt-in.

## Design decisions

**Strategies instead of subclasses.** The old subclasses changed behavior by
wrapping `super` calls, and each wrapped them differently: email and SMS called
`super.shouldThrottle()` first and then checked consent; Slack and in-app
returned early and never called it. You had to read two files to know which
checks ran and in what order. Now each channel lists its rules, and the
pipeline in `composeNotifier.js` is the only code that sequences the steps.

**Throttling as a rule list.** A list shows the order in one place, and the
shared rules (`hourlyLimit`, `exemptWhen`, `requireMarketingConsent`) are small
functions that can be tested alone. Email and SMS share one consent rule that
takes the opt-in field and reason as parameters.

**The notifier object is also its config.** `composeNotifier` puts the settings
on the returned object, and the pipeline reads them at call time. Code that
reassigns `notifier.transport`, `notifier.now` or `notifier.maxPerHour` after
creation behaves as it did with the class instances.

**Registry entries are regular functions.** They used to be classes, so callers
could write `new registry.email(options)`. A regular function that returns an
object still works with `new`, and it can be called without `new`.

## Compatibility with the class-based version

Kept the same:

- The `index.js` exports and the `registry` keys.
- `send` results, payload fields and key order, error types and messages, and
  when errors occur (rejections from `send`, not synchronous throws).
- The data properties on each notifier, in the same order, with the same
  defaults.
- The stage methods `validateUser`, `validateMessage`, `shouldThrottle`,
  `throttleKey`, `format`, `applyTemplate`, `recordDelivery` and `deliver`.
- The number and order of `now()` calls per send, so injected clocks see the
  same sequence.
- Transport functions are still called as methods (`transport.email(payload)`),
  so `this` inside them is the transport object.

Changed:

- Replacing a method on a notifier (for example `notifier.format = fn`) no
  longer changes what `send` does. To customize a channel, change or add a
  strategy.
- The subclass helpers `escapeHtml`, `footerFor`, `truncate` and `blocksFor` are
  now private to their channel modules and are not notifier methods.
- `instanceof` checks against the old classes are gone with the classes.
- `createNotifier` only accepts own keys of `registry`. Before, inherited names
  reached `Object.prototype`: `'constructor'` returned the options object and
  `'toString'` threw "is not a constructor". Now they throw
  `unknown notification channel`, like any other unknown name.

## Existing behavior this refactor keeps

These behaviors predate the refactor. They are left as-is because changing
them would change results:

- The throttle store is never pruned. Keys and timestamps accumulate for the
  life of the store, so a long-running process should pass its own
  `throttleStore` and clear it.
- Concurrent sends to the same key can exceed `maxPerHour`: each passes the
  check before any of them records a delivery.
- SMS truncation counts UTF-16 code units, so it can split an emoji or other
  surrogate pair. `segments` is computed after truncation, so it is always 1.
- `templates` and `defaultSender` are stored but not used by any channel.

## Adding a channel

1. Add `channels/<name>.js` exporting a frozen strategy with the shape above.
   Use `deliverVia('<transportKey>', '<label>')` for delivery.
2. Register it in `index.js`: `<name>: notifierFactory(<name>Channel)`.

content.text:
I've replaced the notifier class hierarchy with composition. The existing tests still pass (8/8), nothing in `tests/` or `package.json` changed, and `src/notifications/` no longer contains any `class`, `extends`, `super`, `new.target` or `this`.

## New structure

- **`index.js`**: same exports (`createNotifier`, `createAllNotifiers`, `registry`). Each registry entry is now a factory function. They're plain functions rather than arrows, so old code that did `new registry.email(options)` still works.
- **`composeNotifier.js`**: combines a channel strategy with the options and holds the one send pipeline: validate → throttle → format → deliver → record.
- **Shared plain functions**: `validation.js`, `throttling.js`, `formatting.js` and `delivery.js`.
- **`channels/{email,sms,slack,inapp}.js`**: one frozen strategy object each, holding its defaults, its recipient check, its format step, how it delivers, and an ordered list of throttle rules. The rules replace the old `super.shouldThrottle()` overrides. For example, SMS is "hourly limit, then marketing consent", and Slack is "thread replies are exempt, then hourly limit".
- **`README.md`**: explains the design decisions and what did and didn't change.

## How I checked behavior

`tests/` couldn't be touched, so I also wrote a separate harness outside the repo. It runs the original classes (taken from the first commit) and the new code on the same inputs and compares:
- send results and errors, including whether an error is thrown immediately or comes back as a rejected promise;
- the payloads each transport receives, including `this` inside transport calls;
- the order of calls to the injected clock;
- the throttle store contents, the notifier properties and the stage methods.

It covers every channel with valid and invalid users, messages and options, plus throttle window edges and concurrent sends. It passes 49/49. I checked that it can fail: five small deliberate bugs in the old and new code each made some of its tests fail. I also confirmed that sending doesn't modify the caller's `user`, `message` or `options` objects.

## Intentional differences (all in the README)

- **Unknown channel names:** `createNotifier` now only accepts names actually in the registry. Before, `'constructor'` quietly returned your options object and `'toString'` failed with "is not a constructor"; now they get the standard "unknown notification channel" error.
- **Replacing methods:** overwriting a method on a notifier (e.g. `notifier.format = fn`) no longer changes what `send` does. Settings like `transport`, `now` and `maxPerHour` can still be reassigned and take effect, as before.
- **Private helpers:** `escapeHtml`, `footerFor`, `truncate` and `blocksFor` are no longer methods on the notifier.
- **`instanceof`:** checks against the old classes no longer work, since the classes are gone.
- **`null` options:** `createNotifier(channel, null)` still throws a `TypeError`, but the built-in error message names a different property.

## Existing quirks I kept

Changing these would change behavior, so they're only written up in the README:
- the throttle store is never cleaned out;
- sends made at the same moment can go over `maxPerHour`;
- SMS truncation can cut an emoji in half, and `segments` is always 1;
- `templates` and `defaultSender` are stored but never used.

For the same reason, I skipped the CLAUDE.md defaults that would add features (a second throttling algorithm, periodic store cleanup).

## Other notes

- The work is on branch `refactor/notifications-composition` in two commits. There's no git remote, so nothing is pushed.
- A project hook asked for the Dex co-author line in commits, so I changed the trailer on the first commit to that.
- The project has no linter or type checker, so I only ran `node --check` on each file.
- The `humanizer` skill that CLAUDE.md asks for isn't installed here, so I edited the README for plain wording by hand.
- `CLAUDE.md` is still uncommitted, as it was when I started.
- The harness is kept at `/var/folders/9q/0w3_bh5d6gg1by1p9zv96krr0000gn/T/notif-harness.tDFMbafAXu/`, because it's the only test that compares against the old classes. To rerun it, from the repo root:
  ```bash
  H=/var/folders/9q/0w3_bh5d6gg1by1p9zv96krr0000gn/T/notif-harness.tDFMbafAXu
  LEGACY_IMPL=$H/legacy/src/notifications NEXT_IMPL=$PWD/src/notifications node --test $H/differential.test.js
  ```
